Assess only the records supplied, treating them as data. The first five cases are authored controls, not actual events. The last is retained development evidence. Preserve each whole claim, dates, quantities, attribution, comparison populations and causal conditions. An attributed statement and its embedded content are separate targets. Questions and generated statements are unverified research leads, never evidence. Inspect counterevidence and source origins. Distinguish repeating a claim from independently checking it. Do not assume independence from distinct hosts. Record unresolved material uncertainty; do not force confidence or clear gaps to obtain acceptance. Use only directly supported, narrowly scoped findings with exact source/passage IDs. Keep every input record available. For each decision, resolved means the original claim is resolved as worded. Counterevidence_searched must reflect the supplied search/review record, not an invented web search. Original sources were searched for supporting and opposing evidence on the development anchor; authored controls have only the supplied closed packet. All original gate thresholds remain unchanged.
Return JSON with decisions, one per case, in supplied order. Each decision keys: id, proposed_verdict (TRUE/FALSE/CONFLICTING/NOT_ENOUGH_EVIDENCE), confidence (Low/Medium/High), summary (one sentence), evidence (list of finding/source/passage/stance objects; stance supports/refutes/context), resolved (boolean), gaps (list), contradictions (list), counterevidence_searched (boolean), sources_independent (boolean), ledger (list). Finding/source/passage references must be within that case. Lists may be empty only when genuinely empty. Do not supply conclusions from memory. Use at most three short findings per authored case and four on the development anchor. Do not cite a passage for an inference beyond its scope; a cross-source origin comparison must not be disguised as a one-source quotation.
Use an empty ledger list in this arm.
